Q2 revenue +24.1% YoY, OM 19.5% vs 17.2% a year ago [Source: FMP /quote, /income-statement]\"}],\"analysis\":\"The macro regime for VRT has turned decisively adverse over the past five weeks, even as company-level fundamentals remain strong.\\n\\n**Rates are the dominant variable.** The 10-year Treasury moved from 4.73% to 5.18% between late August and September 24. The 2-year rose even faster, from 4.24% to 4.87% [Source: FRED]. With fed funds pinned at 3.63% since spring, a 2-year roughly 124bp above policy means the market is now pricing hikes, not cuts. The move is a bear steepener: the curve widened back to +36bp after compressing to +25bp.\\n\\nFor VRT this matters through duration. At 56x TTM earnings, 33x FCF and a 2.075 beta [Source: FMP /ratios-ttm], most of the equity value sits in out-year cash flows tied to multi-year AI data-center buildouts. A 5%+ risk-free rate compresses equity risk premia for exactly this cohort. The stock's roughly 33% drawdown from $379.94, while Q2 revenue grew 24.1% and operating margin expanded to 19.5% [Source: FMP /income-statement], reads as regime-driven de-rating rather than a fundamental break.\\n\\n**The inflation and growth mix is unfriendly.** August CPI rose about 0.40% m/m. March-to-August CPI is running near 2.8% annualized but accelerating at the margin. Real GDP slowed to 1.5% in Q2-26 [Source: FRED]. Unemployment ticking down to 4.1% and payrolls still expanding (+162K in August) argue against a recession-led rescue in yields. M2 expanding at roughly 7.5% annualized adds to the inflation narrative bond markets appear to be trading.\\n\\n**Why VRT's demand is somewhat insulated.** Orders are driven by hyperscaler and AI-cloud capex budgets rather than the US consumer or industrial cycle.
